title: Digital Domain Breaks Down 418 VFX Shots for Spielberg's 'Disclosure Day'
excerpt: Led by VFX supervisor Joel Behrens, the studio's team of nearly 400 artists delivered photoreal aliens, forest animals, a 40-shot train chase, a winter landscape and an overhead crop circle for the Universal sci-fi feature.
content:
Led by VFX supervisor Joel Behrens, the studio's team of nearly 400 artists delivered photoreal aliens, forest animals, a 40-shot train chase, a winter landscape and an overhead crop circle for the Universal sci-fi feature.

Digital Domain has released a VFX breakdown reel for its work on Steven Spielberg's Disclosure Day, the Universal Pictures sci-fi feature that hit theaters June 12. As the film's lead and primary visual effects vendor, the studio delivered 418 final shots with a global team of nearly 400 artists, working under Digital Domain VFX supervisor Joel Behrens.

Following a mandate for authenticity, the studio steered away from stylized science fiction and shaped its work around real-world UFO reports and military FLIR (forward-looking infrared) footage.

That work included photoreal alien entities, a lineup of forest animals and seamless animal transformations, as well as a 40-shot train chase with CG environment extensions. The team also built sprawling digital environments, among them a winter landscape and an overhead crop circle, along with recreations of military UAP - unidentified anomalous phenomena - footage.

The reel includes: a man walking into a wheat field as a blue-tinted pass gives way to the golden crop, before overhead shots reveal him standing at the center of a huge crop circle; a red cardinal settles on a kitchen table at breakfast; a freight train plows into a red car at a level crossing; and a woman walks barefoot through a snowy night forest toward a glowing cottage.

Later shots show a grey alien seated on a television studio set, and a wall of control-room monitors playing infrared targeting footage stamped "Property of Wardex."

To manage the shots across its offices, Digital Domain deployed new pipeline tools, including a brand-new, three-tier Creature Muscle system. Recent studio work also includes IT: Welcome to Derry and The Fantastic Four: First Steps.
